official.deadline_note: Two-step process: eligibility confirmation request due October 2, 2026; references due October 30, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET; complete application due November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET
official.status_note: The Foundation states the 2027 application period runs from September 1 to November 6, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. (ET)
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published value: 'Up to $50,000 per year for three years - To cover tuition and living expenses related to your doctoral studies'
benefits: Up to $50,000 per year for three years, to cover tuition and living expenses related to doctoral studies
Up to $20,000 per year for research and travel, supporting research, networking activities and travel
Mentorship and experiential learning through meetings, masterclasses, seminars and field experiences
Membership of a multidisciplinary community of Scholars, Mentors and Fellows
Access to a network of more than 500 Foundation alumni
eligibility: A Canadian student enrolled at a Canadian university, a Canadian student enrolled at a university outside Canada, or an international student enrolled at a Canadian university
International students residing outside Canada or enrolled at a university outside Canada are not eligible
In the first year of a PhD program at the time of application, or in the second year
Field of study broadly related to the humanities or social sciences and addressing issues relevant to Canada's future
PhD research aligned with at least one of the four themes: Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment
Three letters of reference: one from the PhD supervisor, one from another academic referee, one from a referee outside academia
requirements: Complete the eligibility screening form first; only applicants whose eligibility has been confirmed can access the full application form
Applications that do not meet the eligibility criteria will not be reviewed
Hold an outstanding academic record and demonstrate intellectual curiosity, ambition, leadership potential, commitment to society and impact beyond academia
documents: Eligibility screening form submitted via SmartSimple
Complete 2027 Scholarship application form (available only after eligibility confirmation)
Three letters of reference (PhD supervisor, another academic referee, a referee outside academia)
selection_criteria: Academic excellence supported by an outstanding academic record
Alignment of the research project with the Foundation's mission and its four founding themes
Ability to share knowledge for the benefit of society
Commitment to making a positive impact demonstrated through initiatives, collaborations or achievements
coverage: Living expenses related to doctoral studies
Research and travel (up to $20,000 per year separately)
application_method: Step 1: complete the eligibility screening form at fdnpetf.smartsimple.ca by October 2, 2026
Step 2: once eligibility is confirmed, complete the full 2027 Scholarship application form and submit by November 6, 2026, 5:00 p.m. ET
official.application_route: Two-step online process in SmartSimple: eligibility screening form first, then the full 2027 application, with references due October 30, 2026
official.citizenship_residency: Canadian students at a Canadian or non-Canadian university, or international students enrolled at a Canadian university; international students residing outside Canada are not eligible
official.international_eligibility: International students are eligible only if enrolled at a Canadian university
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Fields broadly related to the humanities or social sciences, addressing issues relevant to Canada's future
official.research_requirement: Research project must align with at least one of the Foundation's four founding themes
official.description: The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation PhD scholarship supports students with an excellent academic record who are engaged in humanities and social sciences research that contributes to the advancement of Canada and society. It is designed for doctoral students who want to go beyond academia, grow through mentorship, and contribute to major societal issues through their research.
official.program_type: Doctoral scholarship for first- or second-year PhD students in the humanities and social sciences

verification.notes: Scholarship value page, Become a Scholar eligibility page and 2027 Applications dates page were all read directly on trudeaufoundation.ca; amounts are 'up to' caps, so fully_funded was left false despite the stated tuition-and-living purpose.

applicant_utility.summary: The Foundation pays up to $50,000 per year for three years explicitly to cover tuition and living expenses, plus up to $20,000 per year for research and travel - among the most generous doctoral packages in Canada, and it funds mentorship and a 500-strong alumni network rather than money alone. The hard gate is a two-step application: your eligibility screening form is due October 2, 2026, months before the November 6, 2026 final deadline, and references must be in by October 30. Research must map explicitly onto one of the four founding themes, so a brilliant project with no stated theme link will struggle regardless of your record.
applicant_utility.best_fit: First- or second-year humanities and social sciences PhD students at a Canadian university, or Canadian doctoral students anywhere, whose research clearly serves one of the four themes and who can evidence engagement beyond academia.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the SmartSimple eligibility screening form well before October 2, 2026 - this gate controls access to the full form
Identify which of the four founding themes your research serves and state it explicitly rather than implicitly
Line up the three referees early: supervisor, a second academic, and one from outside academia
Confirm references will be received by October 30, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET
Budget the full application for submission before November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET
common_rejection_risks: Missing the October 2 eligibility-confirmation deadline and never gaining access to the application form
Applying when you are outside Canada and not enrolled at a Canadian university
Being in year three or beyond of the PhD, outside the first-or-second-year window
A research proposal with no demonstrable tie to any of the four themes
References arriving after the October 30 cutoff regardless of application quality
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The scholarship is capped at 'up to' $50,000 per year, so if tuition at your institution plus living costs exceed the cap the shortfall is yours to fund; dependants' costs and relocation are not addressed.
document_audit: One referee must be outside academia - many applicants submit three academics and breach the rule
The eligibility screening form uses SmartSimple; identity and enrolment details must match your university records exactly
The full form only unlocks after eligibility confirmation, so do not delay step one while perfecting step two
alerts: Mandatory information sessions run in the weeks of October 5 and October 12, 2026 - attend one even if it feels optional
Applications failing the eligibility criteria are not reviewed at all, so self-check every bullet first
Award amounts are ceilings, not guarantees; the Foundation publishes no per-candidate award schedule
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: SmartSimple two-step route: eligibility screening form by October 2, 2026, then the full 2027 application by November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET, with references submitted by October 30.
